q: what is the capital of egypt
a: The capital of Egypt is Cairo, the largest city in the Middle East and Africa, with a metropolitan population of over 21 million. Cairo sits on the Nile River, near the ancient site of Memphis and the Giza pyramid complex, whose Great Pyramid of Khufu is the last surviving wonder of the ancient world. The city was founded in 969 CE by the Fatimid dynasty and grew into a major center of Islamic scholarship, home to Al-Azhar University, founded in 970, one of the oldest universities in the world. Egypt's government and parliament are headquartered in Cairo, though a new administrative capital is being built about 45 kilometers east of the city.

q: what is the capital of brazil
a: The capital of Brazil is Brasília, a planned city inaugurated as the federal capital on 21 April 1960. It was built from scratch in the central highlands under President Juscelino Kubitschek, designed by architect Oscar Niemeyer and urban planner Lúcio Costa, with a distinctive airplane or bird shape when seen from above. Brasília was chosen to move the capital inland from Rio de Janeiro, the previous capital, to encourage development of Brazil's interior. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, one of the largest planned cities in the world, and today it houses the National Congress, the Planalto Palace, and the Supreme Federal Court, all icons of modern architecture.

q: what is the capital of mexico
a: The capital of Mexico is Mexico City (Ciudad de México), one of the largest metropolitan areas in the world with over 21 million people in the metro region. It was built on the ruins of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital, which the Spanish under Hernán Cortés conquered in 1521. The city sits in the Valley of Mexico at about 2,240 meters (7,350 feet) above sea level, on a former lake bed, which causes the sinking of many historic buildings and occasional seismic vulnerability. Mexico City is the political, cultural, and economic heart of the country, home to the Zócalo (main square), the Palacio Nacional, the Metropolitan Cathedral, and one of the world's great art museums, the Palacio de Bellas Artes. It hosts the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), one of Latin America's premier universities.

q: what is the capital of nigeria
a: The capital of Nigeria is Abuja, which replaced Lagos as the federal capital on 12 December 1991. Abuja was a purpose-built city, chosen for its central location in the country — at the geographic and ethnic crossroads of Nigeria's diverse population — and its moderate climate. It was designed by the American planner Kenzo Tange and other international architects, with the impressive Nigerian National Mosque, National Christian Centre, and the three-armed Aso Rock presidential complex forming its landmark skyline. Nigeria's largest city and commercial hub remains Lagos, on the Atlantic coast, which is one of Africa's biggest and fastest-growing cities, with an estimated metro population exceeding 15 million.

q: what is the capital of turkey
a: The capital of Turkey is Ankara, which replaced Istanbul as the capital in 1923 when Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founded the modern Republic of Turkey. Ankara is located in the central Anatolian plateau and was chosen for its central position, away from the coast and the imperial legacy of Istanbul, to anchor the new republic's identity. Today it is Turkey's second-largest city with about 5.7 million people and is the seat of government, the Grand National Assembly, and foreign embassies. Istanbul, the former capital of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires and the country's largest city, straddling Europe and Asia on the Bosporus, remains the economic and cultural heart of the nation.

q: what is the capital of south korea
a: The capital of South Korea is Seoul, one of the world's great megacities with over 9.4 million people in the city proper and more than 25 million in the wider capital region, the second-largest urban agglomeration in the world. Seoul has been the capital of Korea for over 600 years, since the Joseon dynasty made it the seat of power in 1394. It is a global technology and culture hub, home to headquarters of Samsung, LG, and Hyundai, and to K-pop and K-drama industries. Historic landmarks like Gyeongbokgung Palace and the Bukchon Hanok Village sit alongside ultra-modern districts such as Gangnam. Seoul was devastated during the Korean War (1950-53) and rebuilt into one of the world's most dynamic economies, with the Han River flowing through its center.

q: what is the capital of argentina
a: The capital of Argentina is Buenos Aires, the country's largest city with about 3 million people in the city proper and over 15 million in the metropolitan area, one of the biggest urban regions in the Americas. Founded in 1536 and refounded in 1580, the city sits on the Río de la Plata estuary and became a global port feeding Argentina's agricultural exports. Known as the 'Paris of South America' for its European-style architecture, Buenos Aires is the birthplace of tango, home to the Teatro Colón opera house, and famed for its neighborhoods like La Boca and Palermo. It is also a center of football culture, with rivals Boca Juniors and River Plate. Politically, the Casa Rosada presidential palace faces the Plaza de Mayo, the stage of Argentina's defining political moments.

q: what is the capital of portugal
a: The capital of Portugal is Lisbon (Lisboa), one of the oldest cities in Western Europe, predating Rome by centuries. With about 545,000 people in the city proper and nearly 3 million in the metro area, it sits on seven hills at the mouth of the Tagus River, opening onto the Atlantic. Lisbon was the center of the Portuguese Age of Discovery — Vasco da Gama sailed from here to India in 1497 — and its Belém district commemorates this era with the Belém Tower and the Monument to the Discoveries. The city was largely rebuilt after the devastating 1755 earthquake. Known for its yellow trams, azulejo tiles, fado music, and vibrant nightlife in neighborhoods like Alfama and Bairro Alto, Lisbon has become one of Europe's most popular destinations.

q: what is the capital of sweden
a: The capital of Sweden is Stockholm, built across 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea, earning it the nickname 'Beauty on Water'. With about 980,000 people in the city and 2.4 million in the metro region, it is Sweden's largest city and political, cultural, and economic center. Stockholm was founded in the 13th century, and its medieval old town, Gamla Stan, houses the Royal Palace and the Nobel Museum. The city is known for its modernity and livability, innovative tech scene (it has produced Spotify, Klarna, and Minecraft), and archipelago of some 30,000 islands. It is also the venue for the annual Nobel Prize ceremonies, held at the Stockholm Concert Hall, followed by the banquet at City Hall.

q: what is the capital of poland
a: The capital of Poland is Warsaw (Warszawa), the country's largest city with about 1.9 million people. Situated on the Vistula River, Warsaw became the capital of Poland in 1596, when King Sigismund III moved the court from Kraków. The city was almost completely destroyed during World War II — the 1944 Warsaw Uprising and subsequent German reprisals left over 85% of the city in ruins — and was rebuilt with extraordinary effort, including the meticulous reconstruction of the Old Town, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Today Warsaw is a thriving economic and cultural capital, with a modern skyline led by the Palace of Culture and Science, and it is the seat of the Polish parliament and government. It is also the birthplace of composer Frédéric Chopin.

q: what is the most populous country
most populous country in the world
which country has the most people
a: As of 2023, India became the most populous country in the world, surpassing China, with a population of about 1.43 billion people. China is second with roughly 1.41 billion. These two nations together account for over a third of humanity. The United States is third with about 335 million, followed by Indonesia (about 277 million) and Pakistan (about 240 million). India's population is still growing, though its fertility rate has fallen below replacement level, while China's population has begun to decline. By some projections, India's population will peak around 2060 at about 1.7 billion before slowly declining.

q: how many countries are in the world
number of countries in the world
a: There are 195 recognized countries in the world today: 193 member states of the United Nations plus two non-member observer states, the Holy See (Vatican City) and Palestine. If you count Taiwan, which operates as a de facto independent state but is not UN-recognized, the number is 196. Other partially recognized or disputed territories, such as Kosovo, Western Sahara, and Northern Cyprus, are recognized by some countries but not by the UN. This is why you'll see figures like 195, 196, or 197 depending on the source. The newest country is South Sudan, which became independent in 2011.

Roughly 1.5 billion people speak English worldwide, but only about 375-400 million of them are native speakers — the rest speak it as a second or foreign language. This makes English the most widely spoken language in the world when all speakers are counted, and the third most common by native speakers alone, behind Mandarin Chinese (about 920 million native speakers) and Hindi (about 345 million). English is an official language in over 50 countries and is the dominant language of international business, science, aviation, and the internet, with an estimated 55-60% of the world's web content in English. It has been called a global lingua franca, used by billions who share no other common language.
